channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Blasts in Ethiopian capital after government banned drone flights
item.description: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed is due to be sworn in for a new term on Monday after winning elections in June, but faces conflict on multiple fronts as several armed groups have formed an alliance against him. Blasts in Ethiopian capital after government banned drone flights.

item.title: Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists
item.description: Exports of crude oil from the Middle East hit their highest level in September since the war with Iran began, reinforcing a trend of increased supplies despite Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, according to analysis of shipping and commodity market data by industry observers. Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists.

item.title: Georgia Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks On Revered Queen Ketevan
item.description: Georgia summoned Iran’s ambassador after his planned book Georgia has summoned Iran’s ambassador after his plans to publish a personal interpretation of Queen Ketevan’s history sparked criticism from ruling party lawmakers. Revered as a saint in Georgia, Ketevan was tortured and killed in Persia in the 17th century after refusing to renounce Christianity. Georgia Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks On Revered Queen Ketevan.

item.title: Altercation, emergency landing and investigation
item.description: Pictures showed that the aircraft had substantial damage. An emergency descent can be controlled, but in this instance, where descent could have been initiated erratically, there can be severe damage and stress to the crucial flight control surfaces and even the aircraft's tail Altercation, emergency landing and investigation.

item.title: Tbilisi Rebukes Iranian Envoy Over Social Media Post On Canonized Georgian Queen
item.description: Georgia's Foreign Ministry has summoned Iran's ambassador after he announced plans to publish his own research into Queen Ketevan. The 17th-century monarch was tortured and executed in Persia, and the Georgian Orthodox Church venerates her as a saint. Tbilisi Rebukes Iranian Envoy Over Social Media Post On Canonized Georgian Queen.

item.title: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal meets U.S. Trade Representative Greer, discusses trade deal
item.description: While Mr. Goyal did not mention discussing the proposed 100% tariffs the U. S. is looking to levy on India, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal had earlier said “all trade issues” would be discussed during the Minister’s visit to the U. S. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal meets U. S. Trade Representative Greer, discusses trade deal.

item.title: Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny
item.description: For years, Pakistan’s claim that the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan operates from sanctuaries inside Afghanistan produced a familiar exchange: Islamabad accused, Kabul denied, and each new militant attack triggered another round of recrimination. That pattern is becoming harder to sustain. The sanctuary dispute can now be tested against a growing body of evidence rather than competing claims [] The p Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny.

item.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
item.description: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday. Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO.

item.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
item.description: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province. Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp.

item.title: 'Exhausted' Afghan Refugees Get Extension At Camp In Qatar As US Lawmakers Urge Action
item.description: Qatar will keep the Afghan refugee camp open for another nine months after the closure deadline passed, according to Afghan refugees being held at a camp in Qatar have been told it will be kept open for another nine months after a deadline for its closure passed, but they face continuing uncertainty over their fate amid an ongoing bar on entry to the United States.

item.title: Venezuela’s Chavistas lament government’s embrace of Trump
item.description: Diehard Hugo Chávez supporters struggle to comprehend ideological U-turn being executed by Delcy Rodríguez’s interim administrationHe was one of the most passionate propagandists for Hugo Chávez’s Bolivarian revolution: a feisty leftist TV personality who spent more than two decades singing the movement’s praises on his state-funded show, The Razorblade. Mario Silva’s devotion was such that he ofte Venezuela’s Chavistas lament government’s embrace of Trump.

item.title: Daredevil Jaan Roose completes slackline walk high above central Seoul
item.description: Estonian completed first of two attempts to navigate narrow ribbon, 160 metres long and 120 metres high, near the city’s famous Gyeongbokgung palace on ThursdayThe lunchtime crowds drifted slowly back to their offices along central Seoul’s main boulevard, heads up and phones raised to the sky. Daredevil Jaan Roose completes slackline walk high above central Seoul.

item.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad
item.description: Support for white Afrikaners, anti-communism and others reveals how US redefining what qualifies as human rightsWith hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a massive $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner.

item.title: Ukraine Delivers Food By Drone As Russian-Occupied Oleshky Faces Starvation
item.description: Oleshky, a Ukrainian city occupied by Russian forces 9 kilometers from Kherson, is on the brink of a humanitarian catastrophe. Since 2023, the city has been without electricity, gas, or drinking water. Now, Ukrainian teams are airlifting food supplies into the embattled area. Ukraine Delivers Food By Drone As Russian-Occupied Oleshky Faces Starvation.

item.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings
item.description: President announces measures amid anger at authorities over recent murders of womenSouth Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders. Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women. He said police would be reviewing unso.

item.title: MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities
item.description: Institutions have for years turned to China for funding opportunities but national security concerns are mountingMI5 issues spy alert to UK universities over Chinese front company stealing researchThe security alert issued by MI5 regarding a Chinese state-owned conglomerate accused of conducting espionage in the UK reveals the extent to which British intelligence remains concerned about Beijing’s MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities.

item.title: Burundi agrees to receive ‘third-country’ migrant deportees from US
item.description: Burundi joins several other African nations in accepting people deported under Trump’s hardline policyBurundi has agreed to join a clutch of ⁠other African nations in receiving migrants from other countries deported from the US under ⁠Donald Trump’s hardline ⁠immigration ​policy. However, the authorities in Bujumbura, the country’s economic capital, said Burundi will only accept those not accused o Burundi agrees to receive ‘third-country’ migrant deportees from US.

item.title: Palestinians yearn for ‘a return to normal life,’ says top Middle East peace envoy
item.description: Acting UN Special Coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov said Palestinians in Gaza yearn for a return to normal life as the UN pushes to restore utilities and rebuild infrastructure amid severe access restrictions. The effort faces obstacles from damaged roads The UN is continuing efforts to support Palestinians in Gaza amid major challenges to humanitarian access, reconstruction and the restoration of essential services, according to Ramiz Alakbarov, Acting UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process.

item.title: Who gets to shape AI? UN debate centres on power, trust and inclusion
item.description: Artificial Intelligence or AI – and the technology behind it – is moving fast. The question being asked across the world is who gets a seat at the table deciding how it's used and who gets to benefit. Who gets to shape AI? UN debate centres on power, trust and inclusion.

item.title: Storm clouds over Gaza, deadly obstacles face Mexican women rights defenders, Latvia booze ban
item.description: UN teams are racing to protect families in Gaza from the coming rainy season, but restricted access to land and shortages of critical supplies are hampering the effort, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday. Storm clouds over Gaza, deadly obstacles face Mexican women rights defenders, Latvia booze ban.
